result:
PR #253 is finished and marked ready. The device test passed every check we registered in advance, and the Swap regression that had held #88 back did not come back.

**Why session 1 didn't finish:** it didn't fail. It stopped on purpose to wait for CI and the device run, and the handback job resumed it once both were in. That's recorded in `docs/lanes/clrwin88/NOTES.md`.

**Device result:** 13 of 13 checks passed (master `0a4e284536` against master plus the change, `78a9609125`, across three test suites).

| Capture | Before | After | Predicted |
|---|---|---|---|
| ColorIntoZeta_ZB | 131,495 | 10,766 | 10,766 |
| ZetaIntoColor | 102,255 | 71,663 | 71,663 |
| Swap | 165,447 | 165,447 | unchanged |
| Swap_ZB | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| The other 7 captures, including the two from other suites | 0 | 0 | unchanged |

I checked the run files myself rather than relying on the verdict:
- All 11 captures read `ok` in both runs, so none is unreadable. An unreadable capture would also score 0, so this is what makes the Swap_ZB 0 a real 0.
- Neither run log shows partial coverage or the Windows–Linux adb connection fault (`UtilAcceptVsock`) that voids pulls.
- The counter at the changed code shows it ran on the device: 3 declines over 2 frames, as predicted. Unmodified master reaches that code too, which was also predicted.

The comparison report says one run per side can't rule out device randomness. I didn't re-run with three runs, because the only two captures that differ between the runs are the two predicted to move, and both landed exactly on their predicted values.

**Merge:** the branch was 31 commits behind master and the PR conflicted, but only on the generated `nv2a_index.json`. I merged master in rather than rebasing, so the commits the prediction names are still on the branch. I then regenerated the index against the tests checkout it was built from (`6743b6ab16`), and its check passes. Preflight passes on the new head `d2888a0ba0`, and the PR now merges cleanly. The `Files:` line matches the diff, and the PR description has the result.

Pushing the merge started a new CI run on `d2888a0ba0`. The fold job waits for it to pass, so nothing else needs doing on this PR.
